subject: Post-call recap: JSON handshake & function-call POC scope
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@paygrid.com>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.l@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: JSON handshake & function-call POC scope

Hi Sana / Ethan — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record.

High-level pain & goals
- Pain: Your payments reconciliation pipeline struggles with ambiguous webhook payloads and downstream rule execution. Manual mapping is slowing ops and causing false positives on chargebacks.
- Goal: Deliver a deterministic structured output from the inference layer (JSON schema) that the rules engine can consume without brittle parsing.

What we heard about your stack
- Ingest: Kafka -> protobufs -> internal normalization (Java)
- Rules engine: Scala-based engine that expects a strict JSON schema payload (fields: transaction_id, amount_cents, currency, risk_flags[], outcome_action)
- Constraints: sub-200ms median inference latency per transaction, per-region data residency in us-east-1, and strict audit trail for model decisions.

Success criteria (as discussed)
1) Output determinism: identical logical outputs given the same canonical input + seed; schema validation pass rate >= 99.5% on sample set.
2) Latency: P95 end-to-end token production must be <= 200ms for single-transaction requests in US region.
3) Integrability: JSON handshake that maps to your rules engine in <= 2 fields changes per sprint.

Functional/technical asks we committed to
- Redwood will deliver a baseline JSON schema draft (attached: initial-json-schema-proposal.json).
- We'll implement two function-call prototypes during POC: a) inference->structured-output (schema-validated), b) tool-call to your internal enrichment API (auth: short-lived token).
- SE will run a short demo showing schema validation and a canary flow that falls back to a lightweight deterministic parser if validation fails.

Proposed next steps / timeline
- This week: Redwood to share schema draft + mutual action plan (attached) — action: Logan
- Next week: SE deep-dive + sandbox credentials exchange — action: Marissa to schedule SE session and request minimal sample set from PayGrid (10k rows).
- Week of Apr 19: 2-week POC kickoff with success criteria gated in HubSpot.

Questions / open items for PayGrid
- Can you confirm the exact field names that the rules engine uses as source-of-truth? (transaction_id vs txn_id, amount vs amount_cents)
- Do you have retention or logging requirements for intermediate model outputs?

Attachments: initial-json-schema-proposal.json (schema draft), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP milestones)

Thanks — I[0m

Logan Wright

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: JSON handshake & function-call POC scope

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side:

- Field canonicalization: Our rules engine uses transaction_id, amount_cents, currency, and status_code as the minimum required fields. We can provide a sample mapping file; Ethan will attach in the next message.
- Determinism: Very important — we need to be confident that repeated runs over the same input produce byte-for-byte stable JSON for the canonical fields. If theres non-determinism in metadata (timestamps, confidence scores), we need a clear contract about which fields are canonical vs. auxiliary.
- Logging/audit: We need both the final JSON and a redacted version of the prompt/context stored for 90 days for compliance. Does Redwood support configurable KV retention on Private/Dedicated?

POC ask: can Redwood provide a mode that: 1) validates against a strict JSON Schema; 2) emits a deterministic canonical serialization (field ordering + consistent number formats); and 3) optionally signs the payload with a request-specific HMAC for downstream verification? If yes, were comfortable moving to a 2-week POC.

Goal: target start Apr 19. Well get sample data over by Wed EOD (10k rows).

Looping you both in with a couple of tactical asks before the SE call:

- Logan: please iterate the schema draft with two variants: compact (min fields) and verbose (include auxiliary metadata). Label fields as canonical vs. auxiliary in the schema comments so PayGrid can enforce validation.
- Ben: can you surface an SE that can implement deterministic serialization and HMAC signing? Prefer someone familiar with our Dedicated/Private options because PayGrid wants retention control.
- Ops: prepare a short runbook showing how KV cache + prefix caching will be disabled for canonical path during POC (we want repeatability).

I attached call-roles.docx with recommended attendees and timelines. Lets get the SE session on the calendar for Apr 15 or 16.
